person.name: Resad Zacina
person.headline: Geek / Founder / Operator / Venture builder
person.role: Co-Founder & Chief Growth Officer, Ministry of Programming

items.title: You should never forget the people who helped you build the company
items.summary: On Tarik Hamzic and Asim Halilbašić — the operators behind FT high-growth awards, airport runs, and a culture that still sits together as friends.

items.title: Sell. Integrate. Map. Launch. — why foundation-model labs will ship your product
items.summary: Every prompt makes your product better and teaches the labs your market. The pattern: sell, integrate, map, launch. Build a moat or become someone else's blueprint.

items.title: The more AI floods everything, the more people want analog
items.summary: A conversation with his son about whether AI takes over the world — and why live events, real experiences, and analog businesses are the counter-move.

items.title: A masterclass on what true venture building looks like behind the scenes
items.summary: Resad on going from the fundraising trenches to helping take NAGA through the fastest IPO in Germany in 15 years — total immersion, full-cycle support, human-in-the-loop.

items.title: Most teams talk about using AI. Here is a small example that actually shipped.
items.summary: Lightweight Slack agents at MOP — Sara turns project work into status updates automatically. Pick a weekly workflow, automate it, ship, iterate.

items.title: AI-first Spec-Driven Development is now live on 7 MOP teams
items.summary: A painful six-week rollout led by Lejla Imamovic and Elmana Pelko. SDD forces thinking before building. Process change without buy-in is just bureaucracy.

items.title: Your most valuable asset is not money. It is attention.
items.summary: Seven hours of screens, 42-second focus, 10,000 ads a day. He stopped letting algorithms decide what he reads and built an intentional information flow.

items.title: AI made us 3x more productive. It also made us 3x more exhausted.
items.summary: When each task takes less time, you do more tasks. The real skill of the AI era is knowing when something is good enough — then closing the laptop.

items.title: 10.5 years of Ministry of Programming
items.summary: 120 products built, 13+ investments, 500+ people hired, 2× FT1000, 200+ events, €500M+ in shareholder value. Next phase: compounding ownership and platforms.

items.title: Judgment is everything in the AI era
items.summary: AI can crunch data and offer paths. Humans remain responsible for the decisions.

items.title: Speed vs Quality in Product Development: How to Ship Fast Without Breaking Things
items.summary: Winning teams do not choose speed or quality. They define what quality means at each stage, overlap work, and ship with shields instead of certainty.

items.title: What You Should Actually Expect from a Strategic Product Partner in 2025
items.summary: A product partner is not a code vending machine. Ask what they would cut from the MVP. If they have no opinion, keep looking.

items.title: How to Upgrade from a Lovable MVP to a Production-Grade System
items.summary: Three transition paths from no-code MVP to production: hybrid GitHub layer, split backend, or full rewrite — and the industry gates that make rewrite non-optional.

items.title: The horrors of vibe coding
items.summary: A Stockholm startup shipped fast, then left the admin interface exposed. Vibe coding looks like magic until you cannot debug the castle you did not build.

items.title: Spec Driven Development as a Standard
items.summary: The spec is the source of truth. Code is the output. SDD makes the decisions of the first few hours legible — including to the AI doing the work alongside you.
